newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble lower but no Yeltsin operation impact.
newsitem.headline: Rouble lower but no Yeltsin operation impact.

text.p: The rouble edged down in calm trading on Friday on bank client selling and dealers said the market, tightly controlled by the central bank, was unaffected by news President Boris Yeltsin would have heart surgery.
Yeltsin said on Thursday he would have a heart operation, probably at the end of September in Moscow. Interfax news agency quoted a senior doctor saying it would be heart bypass surgery.
"This news cannot affect the interbank and currency exchange markets as the central bank controls them strictly," Avtobank dealer Sergei Gornev said.
Another dealer said trading had become as usual less active after the dollar approached the central bank's dollar offer rate.
Gornev said client orders formed the main part of trading as rate for today and tomorrow settlement were almost the same and rouble funds were cheap.
"There is no scope for speculation in such a situation," he said.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,371-74 per dollar compared with an early 5,369-72 and 5,368-71 late on Thursday. Tomorrow roubles edged down to 5,373-76 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,367-70.
The central bank said it had set 5,336-5,376 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Friday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 10-15 percent compared with Thursday's late 10-20 percent.
